title: Tallulah chasing Bechet and Rose as chaperone
summary: Rose tells how Tallulah pursued Bechet from city to city and he was elected chaperone; Bechet was a tightwad but reliable on jobs.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: Didn't he have women that were bothering him?
Yeah, you don't want me to tell you about Tallulah. Well, that's up to you.
Well, of course, I've written that for a book. Okay. But Tallulah was just crazy about Sidney and used to chase him around all the time from city to city.
What was his attitude towards Shaker, though?

Well, Sidney really didn't care that much. He was interested in Tallulah, I think, because Tallulah gave him money and gifts of various kinds. And she never seemed to miss an opportunity to find out where he was playing. And, of course, I was always involved to the extent that if they were going to go anyplace together, somebody had to be along to make it look respectable. So I was elected for that.

Kind of a chaperone. Sorry, I find that funny. He was a notorious tightwad. Never spent any money. But one time he did give me a clasp for my necktie, which I eventually gave to Walt Gower, who plays clarinet for the Mother's Boys in Detroit. And he was very reliable on jobs. That is, he was always where he was supposed to be at the time he was supposed to be there. And never seemed to be paying much attention to the other musicians or what they were doing. And was extremely uncritical of other musicians.
